segment_objections.objection: We already moved to a custom SMTP provider and still get 429 email rate limit exceeded on signup, so changing sender again will not fix it.
segment_objections.answer: Loops documents two connection paths for Supabase auth email (Send Email Hook or SMTP) and its own sending rates of 10 emails per second on Free and up to 1,000 per second per team on paid plans; the selected evidence does not establish any change to the auth platform's own auth-email rate limit, which remains a Supabase-side setting.

segment_objections.objection: Will every auth email type actually come from us, or will some silently revert to the platform's sender?
segment_objections.answer: With the Send Email Hook each auth email type gets its own Loops template and the path is documented as covering every type including security notifications, but any type without a Loops template falls back to Supabase's own sender and unmapped action types are silently skipped in the documented implementation.

segment_objections.objection: We are on Clerk, not Supabase — can Loops take over our authentication emails?
segment_objections.answer: No; the documentation states Loops reads Clerk webhook events to sync contacts and start workflows while Clerk keeps sending its own authentication emails, so on Clerk the supported part is contact sync and the onboarding sequence.

segment_objections.objection: Last time we switched the send path it broke and reverting left auth email failing, so this is a risky change right before launch.
segment_objections.answer: Both Loops paths use the same Loops transactional emails, so a team can start with SMTP and switch to the hook later without rebuilding templates; the documented SMTP requirement is that at least Confirm signup and Magic Link templates exist, with Confirm signup variables also available in Magic Link, or emails will not be sent.

segment_objections.objection: How much DNS and domain work does this add to a launch that is already blocked?
segment_objections.answer: Sending requires a verified Loops sending domain, with SPF, DKIM, MX and DMARC records copied or exported into the DNS provider and a subdomain such as mail.yourcompany.com recommended; DKIM signing is active from the first send once those records are in place.
